newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five more killed in Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Five more killed in Karachi violence.

text.p: At least five people were killed in violence overnight in Pakistan's industrial port city of Karachi, police said on Sunday.

Mohammad Islam and Aftab were shot dead in the Mahmoodabad area in District East, Safeer Ahmed was shot dead in Saeedabad and Abdul Tahir, 35, was shot and killed in PIB Colony in District East. An unidentified 26-year-old man was killed in Orangi in District West, they said.

In addition, police said the decomposed body of an unidentified young man had been found in a coastal area of District West on Sunday. He had apparently died about two weeks ago, but the cause of his death was not immediately known.
No group claimed responsibility for the latest killings.
Violence has surged in Karachi in recent weeks amid renewed feuding between militants of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its MQM-Haqiqi splinter faction.
At least 110 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi this year, compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.
The MQM was brought into a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after national and provincial elections in February.
